fullName.en: Aérospatiale SA342M Gazelle (French Army anti-tank helicopter)

tagline.en: The fast, glass-nosed French scout that introduced the Fenestron

summary.en: The Gazelle is a light five-seat helicopter designed by Sud Aviation and built by Aérospatiale, first flown in 1967. It was the first production helicopter with a Fenestron, a fan-in-fin tail rotor. The SA342M is the French Army (ALAT) anti-tank version: a single Turbomeca Astazou XIV M engine, four HOT wire-guided missiles and a roof sight for the gunner. Upgraded SA342M1 Viviane machines added a thermal night sight and are still in service.

en: 1 × Turbomeca Astazou XIV M turboshaft, about 870 hp max

desc.en: Three blades turning on a 10.5 m rotor disc. Upgraded Viviane-standard Gazelles use heavier-duty Écureuil (AS355/AS555 Fennec) blades to cope with the higher weight.
The hub holds the three blades and changes their pitch through the swashplate, which is how the pilot climbs, descends and steers.
Slows the engine's high-speed output down to rotor speed and drives both the main rotor mast and the tail drive shaft.
A single turboshaft engine mounted openly behind the gearbox under a slim cowling. It runs at a constant 43,000 rpm and is rated at about 870 hp maximum.
The gunner's stabilised sight above the cabin. On the SA342M1 Viviane it adds a thermal camera and laser rangefinder for night firing of HOT missiles.
The large curved 'glasshouse' windows give the two crew an almost all-round view, which matters for low-level scouting.
The main structure carrying the crew seats, controls and fuel. It seats a pilot plus up to four passengers.
Side mounts that carry the armament. The SA342M's main weapon is four wire-guided HOT anti-tank missiles with a range of about 4 km.
A slender tube that carries the tail drive shaft back to the Fenestron and holds the tail surfaces.
Small fixed wings with end fins that keep the helicopter steady in pitch and yaw during fast forward flight.
A 13-blade fan inside the tail fin, 0.69 m across, spinning at about 5,800 rpm. The Gazelle was the first production helicopter with a Fenestron, which is safer and quieter than an open tail rotor.
Simple tubular skids instead of wheels: light, strong and able to land on rough or uneven ground.

note.en: Rendered from a third-party 3D model. Labels describe the real SA342M Gazelle; the model is not an exact replica.
